title: Sparkdrift India
subtitle: A cel-shaded kart racer across India, built in the browser
caveats: No side-by-side against Mario Kart 8 Deluxe is possible — the game is not available in this environment. The critic works from a written first-party rubric applied to our own captured frames.
Multiplayer is local split-screen. Online play needs an authoritative server, prediction and hosting, none of which exist here.
Frame timings come from a headless software rasteriser with no GPU. They bound the CPU cost only and say nothing about real device frame rate.

pieces.name: India worldbuilding
pieces.note: Eight tracks across Kerala, Jaipur, Mumbai, the Himalaya, Goa, Varanasi, Kutch and Bengaluru. Two cups of four.

pieces.name: Visual quality
pieces.note: Lighting, shadows, sky, particles, line weight and grade. The biggest gap to a first-party bar.

pieces.name: Roster and customization
pieces.note: Medical-student cast with honest stat trade-offs; driver, frame, wheels, paint, number.

pieces.name: Defect sweep
pieces.note: Respawn never triggers from a deep off-track placement; one AI kart stays off the corridor for 1.43 s.

pieces.name: Split-screen
pieces.note: Two to four players, per-viewport cameras and HUDs.

pieces.name: Items and balance
pieces.note: Position-weighted draw, counterplay, and a hundred-race balance table actually read.

pieces.name: Menus and shell
pieces.note: Title, cup select, character select, results, options, licences.

pieces.name: Audio and music
pieces.note: Synthesised throughout, with Indian instrumentation per cup.

foundation.name: Track spine
foundation.note: Legs-and-fillets centreline, exact closure, one surfaceAt() queried by everything, swept mesh from the same stations.

foundation.name: Vehicle
foundation.note: Four raycast wheels, spring and damper, grip circle, slip-gated drift charge in three tiers.

foundation.name: Collision
foundation.note: Barriers are half-planes in track space, so the clamp is an exact swept test at any speed.

foundation.name: Verification
foundation.note: Playwright harness driving the production build; named frames each stating what they prove.

critic.verdict: Not yet run. The first critic pass goes in once wave 1 lands.

fixed: The cel shader multiplied by the light colour as well as the band level, darkening every surface by the ambient's own luminance.
Nothing converted linear to sRGB on output — the whole game rendered about five stops too dark.
The mesh builder's winding was inverted, so every generated box was inside-out and back-face culled. Karts rendered as solid black shells.
The Sobel's relative depth test fired across the entire road, because a grazing surface has a large depth gradient by construction.
A jump ramp launched at 31° for 102 m, clear over its landing. Caught by the validator's ballistic probe, not by eye.
